name: Mandate
description: Consent for generative media on DKG v10. A depicted person's agent publishes a likeness grant; a rendering agent resolves it before invoking an identity-bearing model and refuses without it; revocations propagate from the graph; anyone can verify a delivered file from its bytes.

install.usageHint: Run one DKG node per party. Set MANDATE_GRANTS_CG to the grantor's registered graph and MANDATE_DERIVATIONS_CG to the producer's (see .env.example), then: mandate status, mandate grant, mandate render, mandate revoke, mandate verify --url <file>.

networkEgress: agent.livepeer.org — Livepeer Agent MCP; only for render --execute and consent capture
operator-supplied media URLs — fetched to SHA-256 the bytes when verifying or recording a derivation
writeAuthority: POST /api/knowledge-assets (create a draft: grant, revocation, or derivation)
POST /api/knowledge-assets/{name}/swm/share (Curator SHARE; retried, because create-with-share is not atomic)
POST /api/knowledge-assets/{name}/vm/publish (Curator PUBLISH to Verifiable Memory; synchronous route only, never publish-async)
POST /api/context-graph/create (one-time operator setup via the dkg CLI; not called by the package)
POST /api/context-graph/register (one-time operator setup via the dkg CLI; on-chain registration)
POST /api/context-graph/subscribe (one-time operator setup via the dkg CLI)
credentialsHandled: LIVEPEER_AGENT_KEY (optional; the keyless demo tier works without it)
security.notes: All DKG access is through the public dkg CLI, resolved via the bin entry @origintrail-official/dkg declares, and the node HTTP API; no internal packages are imported and nothing is written to SPARQL directly. Each node's API token is read from its own DKG_HOME and sent only to that local node; wallet keystores are never read. Curator PUBLISH is used deliberately: measured on two v10.0.16 testnet nodes, Shared Working Memory for these context graphs did not reach the other party (the grantor node logged RFC-64 authority bootstrap incomplete, ERC721NonexistentToken), so a revocation left in SWM was never seen by the producer, which kept permitting. Once anchored, the producer's own node refused within 4 to 49 seconds across three runs. Each party publishes only to a context graph it registered itself. The package has no install scripts, its core has zero runtime dependencies, and npm audit --omit=dev is clean. 0.1.0 was published from a local machine and carries no provenance attestation.

promotionPath: Drafts are written and finalized in Working Memory on the authoring node; consent media, reference images, names and prompts never leave it. The finalized clause data is shared to the owner's context graph and then published to Verifiable Memory, because cross-party consent only works once anchored: grants and revocations in the grantor's graph, derivation edges in the producer's. The resulting UALs let any subscribed node or oracle resolve whether a render was authorised, and whether that authorisation still stands, without trusting either party.
